definition: An approach often described as 'learning to learn,' where a model is trained across many tasks so that it can adapt quickly to new, related tasks with minimal additional data.
details: Meta-learning is closely related to few-shot learning, and has influenced how researchers think about the in-context learning capabilities that emerge in large language models.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. Here is the short version: An approach often described as 'learning to learn,' where a model is trained across many tasks so that it can adapt quickly to new, related tasks with minimal additional data. The part that makes it sing: Meta-learning is closely related to few-shot learning, and has influenced how researchers think about the in-context learning capabilities that emerge in large language models. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. And that is Meta-Learning — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
